assumptions: CONDITIONAL proposal only. These bindings do not approve semantic equivalence.
Both controls concern the same fund, assessment occasion and applicable circular. Commencement and the governing assessment date are not established by this packet.

Both original outputs explicitly use TRUE_IS_SATISFIED: true denotes satisfaction of a classification trigger, not prohibition or compliance. The required output enum cannot express that convention. The two TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT entries below are schema-only placeholders, not semantic bindings; this proposal is blocked from operative use unless the schema supports TRUE_IS_SATISFIED. No source-supported conversion to either permitted output convention is established.

Common facts are Boolean propositions with separately preserved evidence states: established true, established false, unknown or conflicting. Unknown and conflicting evidence must not be coerced into Boolean values or silently resolved by a binding.

Bindings are conditional on matching evidence, asset definitions, assessment basis and timing on both sides. Disagreement in those matters remains unresolved rather than being erased by common fact names.

The exposure fact requires a supported common methodology for total direct and indirect exposure and NAV. The packet does not establish a complete measurement protocol; illustrative holdings, permitted exposure and disclosure examples cannot supply one.
Private market assets means private credit and private equity. The listed forms of indirect exposure are non-exhaustive.

An operative designation requires evidence of an actual SFC decision applicable at the assessment occasion. Possible designation, adverse risk factors, consultation, scrutiny and missing records neither establish nor negate a designation. Continued designation or declassification after an exposure change is not settled here.

Both scopes derive as (and common_public_sfc_authorised (not common_is_laf)). Established false scope yields no classification decision under this control, not a false classification result. Unresolved or conflicting scope must remain flagged.

For established in-scope funds, both proposed results derive as (or common_exposure_at_least_50_percent common_operative_sfc_designation). An established true route can determine satisfaction despite an unknown other route; false requires both routes established false. Conflicting evidence remains explicitly flagged and cannot be represented as an uncontested Boolean determination.
Classification does not establish compliance with resulting sale requirements, general non-complex status, or treatment under excluded or missing instruments.

common_facts.meaning: Whether the same assessed fund is authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong at the common assessment occasion.
common_facts.name: common_public_sfc_authorised

common_facts.meaning: Whether the assessed fund is a listed closed-ended alternative asset fund within the circular's footnote 6 exclusion.
common_facts.name: common_is_laf

common_facts.meaning: Whether total direct and indirect exposure to private credit and private equity amounts to at least 50% of the assessed fund's NAV at the common assessment occasion, conditional on a supported common measurement basis. Unresolved methodology, missing evidence or conflicting evidence is preserved separately.
common_facts.name: common_exposure_at_least_50_percent
common_facts.unit: Boolean; inclusive threshold of 50 percent of NAV

common_facts.meaning: Whether an actual SFC case-by-case designation of the assessed fund as a complex product under this circular applies at the common assessment occasion. Possibility of designation and absence of records do not establish either truth value; unresolved duration or conflicting evidence remains separately flagged.
common_facts.name: common_operative_sfc_designation

evidence.quote: funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6
6 Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs).
private credit and private equity (collectively, private market assets)
A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV.
On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.
2 The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.

A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.
